title: The one open door in the dark age
hookLine: the Bhagavata forecasts an age of stand-ins, then opens one door
carry: in the kali age, sing the name
tomorrow: after Kalki, what's the first sign that a new age has begun?
last: GOD'S COMING ISN'T FINISHED: KALKI WILL BE: WILL BE.

lines: WEALTH FOR BIRTH. MIGHT FOR RIGHT.
cards: Scroll any comment section long enough and the complaints start to rhyme: money buys respect, the loudest one wins, a costume passes for the real thing. Here's an older version. Wealth will count as good birth.
Might will decide what's just. A thread worn on the body will be enough to call someone a Brahmin. Being clever with words will pass for learning.
It sounds like today because it's built from the same complaint. It's the Bhagavata Purana, forecasting the age Kalki is born into.

teach.b: The Bhagavata's last book opens like this: day by day, under the force of time, truthfulness, mercy and patience will wear thin, and even strength and memory with them. Then comes that list. Notice what it's really about.
Stand-ins: money standing in for good character, a thread standing in for a Brahmin's life, smooth talk standing in for learning, strength standing in for justice.
The Kali age, as the Bhagavata draws it, is an age of substitutes.

teach.h: KALI THE AGE, KALI THE GODDESS: TWO WORDS.
teach.b: One thing to hear clearly: Kali, the age, isn't Kālī, the goddess. They're two different Sanskrit words, with short vowels for the age and long ones for the goddess. And now the turn, and it's a sound.

teach.h: ONE GREAT GOOD: SINGING THE NAME.
teach.b: The same book, after all that gloom, says the Kali age is an ocean of faults with one great good: simply by singing Krishna's name, a person can be set free.
That singing is kirtan, sometimes one voice leading a line and a whole room answering it.

teach.h: IN THE KALI AGE, SING THE NAME.
teach.b: That verse is one reason many Hindus, Vaishnavas above all, gather to sing the same names for hours. In an age of stand-ins, the Bhagavata points to something plain: a voice, saying a name, again and again.

how: Kirtan and bhajan evenings, singing names of God together, sometimes as call and response, are held in temples and homes, and some Vaishnavas point to the Bhagavata's verse on the Kali age's one great good.

o: the goddess whose name the dark age carries
the one promised to an age of stand-ins
the singer who leads the room in kirtan

p: stands in for a Brahmin's life

s: the dark age, Kali, is named after the goddess Kālī
two different Sanskrit words: short vowels for the age, long ones for the goddess.
the Bhagavata's forecast is about stand-ins, like wealth passing for good birth
the forecast is mainly about floods, monsters and fire from the sky
it's about truth and mercy wearing thin, and stand-ins taking their place.

games.q: an account with a verified badge and a huge following posts like an expert, with no real knowledge behind it. by the Bhagavata's forecast, what's going on?
o: a stand-in: the badge is passing for the learning it's meant to mark.
nothing odd: a huge following is a fair sign of real learning.
the Kali age just means nobody can really know anything for sure.
games.why: the forecast lists stand-ins: a thread for a Brahmin's life, clever talk for learning. The mark isn't the thing it marks.

practice: Choose one word that matters to you, a name of God if you pray, or a word like peace if you don't, and say it softly on each breath out. Keep your voice low and even, the way a room answers a leader's line.
For the last part of the sit, just listen to the quiet after it.

wordCard.voice: Kalki: promised in the Bhagavata to the Kali age, an age of stand-ins with one door left open.

orig.note: Sanskrit kali, the age, with short vowels; the goddess is Kālī, काली, with long ones.

carryVoice: Your line: in the Kali age, sing the name. Kalki is promised to a hard age, and the age still has an open door. More tomorrow.
